jobs.title: Director of Data Architecture
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director of Data Architecture based in Canada.

The Director of Data Architecture will define and lead the organization's long-term data strategy, overseeing the architecture, infrastructure, and teams responsible for managing its entire data ecosystem. You will drive the development of scalable data platforms, ensuring seamless data integration, transformation, storage, and delivery across multiple systems. Leading two specialized functions, Data Engineering and Data Operations Engineering, you will balance innovation with the reliability and performance of existing production environments. This position combines strategic leadership with hands-on technical involvement, particularly during the initial stages of team development. You will work closely with executive and engineering leaders to establish architectural standards and align data initiatives with broader business objectives. You will also play a central role in strengthening data quality, governance, security, and compliance while building a robust data foundation that supports analytics, product innovation, and business growth.

Accountabilities

Define and lead the long-term data architecture and platform strategy, overseeing data warehouses, operational data stores, and the evolution toward a modern medallion-based lakehouse architecture (bronze, silver, and gold layers).
Design, develop, and manage data lake and warehouse infrastructure, including the creation and optimization of data marts supporting analytics, product development, and business reporting.
Establish architecture standards and orchestration strategies for all data workflows, including source ingestion, web-scraping pipelines, ETL/ELT processes, and automated workflow management.
Oversee the infrastructure, administration, capacity planning, reliability, and cost optimization of data warehouses and pipelines.
Develop and enforce comprehensive data governance frameworks covering data quality, lineage, access controls, classification, retention, and auditability.
Build, lead, and scale two complementary teams: Data Engineering, responsible for developing new pipelines and architecture, and Data Operations Engineering, responsible for maintaining and optimizing existing production processes.
Define the organizational structure and leadership model as the teams grow, determining when additional management layers and operational responsibilities are required.
Remain hands-on during the initial stages by designing and reviewing pipelines, data models, and orchestration processes, while progressively empowering teams to manage execution independently.
Maintain strong technical oversight to guide architectural decisions and ensure the continuous evolution of the data platform.
Collaborate with engineering leadership and the CTO to establish technical direction, align data architecture with company-wide standards, and support strategic technology decisions.
Partner with product, analytics, data engineering, and business stakeholders to understand data requirements and translate them into effective warehouse and data mart solutions.
Establish and monitor data quality controls, lineage tracking, and auditability standards across all data pipelines.
Oversee data access policies, classification standards, and retention practices to ensure secure and compliant data management.
Ensure that compliance-sensitive and audit-relevant information is managed appropriately as data sources and customer requirements expand.

Requirements

At least 10 years of professional experience in data engineering, data architecture, or related technical fields, including a minimum of 5 years in Director- or Manager-level leadership positions with responsibility for architecture strategy and team management.
Extensive hands-on experience designing, implementing, and operating cloud-based data warehouse or lakehouse architectures, particularly with Snowflake and/or BigQuery.
Strong understanding and practical experience with medallion architecture patterns, including bronze, silver, and gold data layers.
Experience integrating multiple source systems, including MongoDB, PostgreSQL, and MySQL, and developing ingestion and ETL pipelines from diverse structured and unstructured data sources.
Experience building and managing web-scraping pipelines, background processing systems, and automated workflow orchestration.
Proven ability to establish, develop, and scale data engineering or data platform organizations, including structuring separate engineering and operations functions.
Strong knowledge of data governance frameworks, with experience establishing and enforcing standards for data quality, lineage, access management, and retention in regulated or compliance-sensitive environments.
Demonstrated ability to define technical strategy in collaboration with senior engineering leaders and influence architectural decisions across multiple teams.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to present technical strategy, platform performance, infrastructure costs, and operational risks directly to executive leadership, including the CTO.
Strong strategic thinking, organizational leadership, and problem-solving abilities, combined with the willingness to remain technically involved when needed.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience consolidating, modernizing, or re-architecting data platforms following acquisitions or significant expansions in data sources.
Familiarity with data orchestration and transformation tools such as Airflow and dbt.
Experience designing and managing large-scale web-scraping and crawling infrastructure.
Background developing data marts and self-service analytics platforms for non-technical stakeholders.
Familiarity with data observability and quality monitoring tools such as Monte Carlo, Great Expectations, Soda, or similar solutions.

Benefits

Competitive annual salary: USD 200,000 per year.
Remote work flexibility: Opportunity to work remotely from Canada.
Strategic leadership opportunity: Shape the long-term data architecture and technology strategy of a growing organization.
Team-building experience: Build, lead, and develop two specialized engineering functions while influencing organizational structure and growth.
Technical innovation: Work with modern cloud data platforms, lakehouse architectures, data orchestration, and advanced governance solutions.
Executive collaboration: Partner directly with senior engineering leadership and contribute to high-level technology decisions.
Professional development: Drive large-scale data transformation initiatives while expanding your leadership and technical influence.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Digital Capabilities
jobs.description:
Manulife is transforming how we deliver digital experiences across our businesses and markets. Through Digital Storefront, we are building a portfolio of enterprise digital capabilities that make it easier, faster and more effective for our segments to deliver differentiated, connected experiences for customers.

As Director, Enterprise Digital Capabilities, you will lead a team responsible for the strategy, execution, evolution, adoption and value realization of a portfolio of enterprise common capabilities that support Manulife's digital strategy across Canada, the United States, Asia and Global Wealth & Asset Management.

This is an enterprise product leadership role. You will establish the future-state vision and value proposition for assigned capabilities, understand segment needs and roadmaps, define and continuously evolve the enterprise roadmap, determine MVP and subsequent releases, and work across business, technology, experience and delivery teams to bring capabilities to market.

Working closely with peer capability leaders, you will ensure individual capability roadmaps come together as a cohesive enterprise portfolio aligned to segment strategies and evolving customer and business needs.

You will work closely with the Common Capability Collective, which brings together segment and enterprise stakeholders to identify needs, establish priorities and align investments. You will ensure capabilities solve meaningful business and customer problems, are designed for reuse across Manulife, and continue to evolve based on adoption, performance, emerging technology and changing business needs.

Success is not simply delivering a capability. It is ensuring that capabilities are adopted, generate measurable value and become stronger over time.

Position Responsibilities

Capability Strategy & Vision

Own the strategy, future-state vision and evolution of assigned enterprise digital capabilities.
Define the business and customer problems each capability is intended to solve and articulate a compelling enterprise value proposition.
Establish clear business outcomes, benefits and success measures for each capability.
Maintain an understanding of customer expectations, industry trends, competitive practices and emerging technologies to inform capability direction.
Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize and reuse capabilities across markets and businesses while enabling appropriate market differentiation.
Actively identify and embed opportunities to leverage AI, GenAI and agentic AI within enterprise capabilities and delivery practices to create differentiated customer experiences, accelerate delivery and improve business outcomes.

Roadmap & Product Leadership

Own and continuously evolve multi-year capability roadmaps that translate enterprise strategy into actionable priorities and investments.
Align capability roadmaps with segment strategies, product roadmaps, customer journeys and technology dependencies.
Define MVPs and subsequent releases that balance customer and business value, speed to market, enterprise scalability and technical feasibility.
Translate capability vision and business outcomes into clear requirements, priorities and measurable objectives for delivery teams.
Make informed prioritization and trade-off decisions based on customer value, business value, reuse potential, effort, dependencies and strategic alignment.
Partner with architecture, technology, data, experience, AI and delivery teams to ensure capabilities are designed for enterprise scale, integration and reuse.

Common Capability Collective & Enterprise Alignment

Work with the Common Capability Collective as the primary forum for gathering segment needs, identifying common requirements, establishing priorities and aligning capability investments.
Build strong partnerships across Canada, the United States, Asia, Global Wealth & Asset Management and Global functions to understand their strategies, roadmaps and evolving capability needs.
Identify commonality across segment requirements and translate individual needs into scalable enterprise solutions where appropriate.
Facilitate decisions and trade-offs when priorities differ across markets or businesses.
Maintain transparency on capability priorities, roadmaps, dependencies, delivery progress and value realization.
Ensure segment perspectives remain represented throughout the capability lifecycle—from strategy and design through implementation and ongoing evolution.

Capability Launch, Adoption & Evolution

Lead capabilities from strategy and concept through MVP, launch, adoption and ongoing maturity.
Develop capability rollout and adoption strategies in partnership with segments and delivery teams.
Work with markets and businesses to integrate enterprise capabilities into their digital experiences and roadmaps.
Identify barriers to adoption and work across teams to resolve them.
Establish feedback loops with users, segments and stakeholders to understand how capabilities are performing in practice.
Use adoption data, customer insights, analytics and stakeholder feedback to continuously improve capabilities and identify new opportunities.
Ensure capabilities evolve as customer expectations, segment requirements, technology and enterprise strategy change.

Value Realization & Performance

Define measurable outcomes and KPIs for assigned capabilities before investment and delivery.
Establish baselines and targets that enable Manulife to understand the incremental value created through common capabilities.
Track and report capability adoption, utilization, customer outcomes, business impact, operational efficiency and other relevant measures.
Demonstrate how enterprise capabilities contribute to segment and enterprise objectives.
Use performance data and insights to identify opportunities for optimization, further investment or changes in direction.
Develop clear executive-level reporting on capability performance, value realization, roadmap progress and emerging opportunities.
Ensure investment decisions continue to be grounded in measurable customer and business value.

Team & Portfolio Leadership

Lead, coach and develop a small team of product and capability resources, providing clear direction, priorities and opportunities for growth.
Work closely with peer Directors to manage enterprise digital capabilities as an integrated portfolio, aligning strategies, roadmaps, priorities, dependencies and investment decisions across capabilities.
Identify connections and dependencies across capabilities to ensure they evolve together to enable cohesive customer and business experiences.
Share resources and expertise across the capability portfolio where appropriate, dynamically aligning capacity to the highest-value priorities.
Foster consistent product management practices, ways of working and measures of success across the Enterprise Digital Capabilities team.
Create an environment of collaboration, accountability and continuous improvement across the team.

Enterprise Leadership & Communication

Act as an enterprise advocate and subject-matter leader for assigned capabilities.
Build awareness and understanding of available capabilities and the value they can create for markets and businesses.
Communicate capability vision, strategy, roadmap and value through clear and compelling storytelling tailored to executive, business and technical audiences.
Influence across organizational boundaries and build alignment among stakeholders with different priorities.
Bring together business, experience, data and technology perspectives to drive enterprise decisions.
Champion an enterprise-first mindset while recognizing legitimate market, regulatory and customer differences.
Contribute to the broader evolution of Manulife's enterprise digital capability portfolio and Digital Storefront strategy.

Required Qualifications

8+ years of experience in digital product management, capability management, digital strategy, platform strategy or related disciplines, including experience operating at a senior product leadership level.
Demonstrated experience defining product or capability vision, strategy, value propositions and multi-year roadmaps.
Experience taking digital products or capabilities from concept and MVP through launch, adoption and continuous evolution.
Strong understanding of digital platforms and enterprise capabilities, with the ability to work effectively across business, technology, architecture, data and experience teams.
Demonstrated ability to translate business and customer needs into scalable solutions and actionable product priorities.
Experience defining and measuring product or capability outcomes, including adoption, customer, operational and financial metrics.
Strong analytical skills and demonstrated ability to use data, customer insights and performance metrics to inform decisions and identify opportunities.
Demonstrated people leadership experience, including coaching and developing talent, setting priorities and effectively deploying resources across competing priorities.
Demonstrated ability to lead through both direct accountability and influence, building alignment across teams, peers and senior stakeholders in a complex matrixed organization.
Exceptional stakeholder management and influencing skills, with experience navigating complex, matrixed organizations.
Strong executive communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to simplify complex topics and articulate business value.
Demonstrated ability to build alignment across stakeholders with different priorities and requirements.
Demonstrated experience applying AI, GenAI and agentic AI to product and capability strategy, delivery and evolution—identifying and implementing opportunities to improve customer and business outcomes, accelerate delivery and increase productivity.
AI-first approach to ways of working, with demonstrated use of AI in day-to-day practices to improve analysis, research, planning, decision-making, communication and execution, and an expectation to continuously identify new opportunities to embed AI into how the team operates.
Financial services, insurance or wealth management experience is an asset.

What Success Looks Like

The Director, Enterprise Digital Capabilities will ensure Manulife's common capabilities are not simply technology investments—they are enterprise products that solve meaningful customer and business problems, are adopted across the organization and deliver measurable value.
Success means creating a clear line of sight from segment need → enterprise opportunity → capability vision → roadmap → MVP → adoption → measurable value → continuous evolution.
It also means ensuring individual capabilities do not evolve in isolation. Working with peer capability leaders, the Common Capability Collective and segment partners, the Director will help create an integrated enterprise capability portfolio in which roadmaps, investments, dependencies and resources come together to enable more connected customer experiences and accelerate delivery across Manulife.
Ultimately, the role enables Manulife to build once where it makes sense, reuse at scale, continuously improve and maximize the value of our enterprise digital investments.

We’ll empower you to learn and grow the career you want.

jobs.title: Vice President, Finance & Business Operations
jobs.description:
CONTEXT

At Make-A-Wish^® Canada
, we’re redefining how the world perceives wishes through our transformative new brand platform: Wishes Are Medicine.
Grounded in research, this platform recognizes what we’ve long known to be true — that wishes have measurable healing power. When prescribed alongside medical treatment, wishes reduce stress, elevate endorphins, limit emergency room visits, and deliver lasting health benefits.

With more than 3,500 children still waiting
and a new child diagnosed with a critical illness in Canada every two hours, our mission has never been more urgent — and there are many more prescriptions to fill.

To meet this challenge, we’ve launched our new three-year strategic plan — Wishes Are Medicine: One Team, One Mission
— focused intentionally on financial sustainability, mission impact, and operational excellence. When a child is facing a critical illness, a wish isn’t just a moment of joy — it’s a medically supported turning point. Studies show that children who receive a wish are 2.5 times less likely
to have unplanned hospital visits and 1.9 times less likely
to need the ER, with 100% of physicians agreeing that a wish can be a pivotal moment in treatment.

At Make-A-Wish Canada, you can play a lead role in bringing these powerful prescriptions to life. Where Wishes Are Medicine
, transformation becomes a pathway to healing at scale — and this role is your opportunity to architect that future.

Our ambition to reach more children and families requires a strong financial and operational foundation. As Vice President, Finance & Business Operations
, you will help shape that foundation, bringing strategic leadership to financial planning, investments, risk, governance and the services that enable our organization to thrive. You will turn insight into action, strengthen how resources are invested and managed, and help build a more resilient, disciplined and mission-driven organization.

At Make-A-Wish Canada
, you’ll join a team united by a shared mission and an unwavering sense of possibility. Every role — whether advancing fundraising, brand, operations, or technology — helps fuel the same trajectory: transforming how hope and healing come to life for children and families nationwide. If you’re ready to help build a future where every eligible child receives the wish that helps them heal, we invite you to read on.

Role Overview

We’re seeking a Vice President, Finance & Business Operations
, a strategic and forward-thinking leader who will help shape the next chapter of Make-A-Wish Canada. This is more than a finance role; it’s an opportunity to strengthen the financial and operational foundation that will enable our mission to grow sustainably.

As a key member of our Senior Leadership Team, and reporting to the Senior Vice President, Transformation & Operations, you will bring together financial strategy, business operations, analytics, risk and governance to strengthen how we plan, invest and make decisions. You’ll provide the insight and discipline to steward our resources responsibly, improve organizational performance, and build the capabilities needed to support sustainable growth and greater mission impact.

If you bring financial acumen, business curiosity and enterprise thinking, and believe the strongest organizations pair ambition with discipline, this is your opportunity to help build the foundation from which our mission can grow and bring the power of Wishes Are Medicine to more children and families across Canada.

This is a full-time, permanent, hybrid
role. The hiring range is $145,000-$170,000.

What You Will Do

Shape Financial Strategy:
Lead budgeting, forecasting, multi-year financial planning, and financial modelling. Translate insights into scenarios and recommendations that guide sustainable, mission-aligned decisions over a three-to-five-year time horizon.

Steward Assets and Investments:
Oversee financial assets, treasury, and investment portfolio performance in accordance with policy, ensuring disciplined stewardship and informed decision-making.

Strengthen Governance and Reporting:
Provide clear financial reporting to the Board of Directors and Senior Leadership Team, support the Finance & Audit Committee, and ensure sound governance, audit readiness, and compliance with CRA and other regulatory obligations.

Advance Enterprise Risk Management:
Maintain the enterprise risk register, strengthen internal controls, and lead business continuity and disaster recovery planning to protect the organization’s assets, reputation, and long-term sustainability.

Modernize Financial Capability:
Build stronger modelling, analytics, systems, and processes that improve forecasting, performance visibility, operational efficiency, and organizational decision-making.

Lead Business Services:
Oversee property management, leases, contracts, insurance, and related business services. Balance operational efficiency and financial sustainability with investments in organizational capability and a safe, supportive workplace.

Oversee Gift and Donation Administration:
Ensure sound systems and processes for restricted giving, endowments, estates, and other complex giving structures, coordinating closely with development teams to support stewardship and compliance.

Advise and Partner:
Serve as a trusted advisor to the Senior Vice President, Transformation & Operations, the CEO, and leadership colleagues on finance, risk, and business operations. Bring an enterprise lens to strategic planning and execution.

Guide and Develop Talent:
Build, coach, and lead a high-performing Finance and Business Operations team, creating clarity, accountability, collaboration, and opportunities for growth.

Champion One Team Leadership:
Model One Team, One Mission leadership by working across functions and geographies, breaking down silos, celebrating collective wins, and leading with empathy, inclusion, accountability, and purpose.

Represent the Mission:
Act as a visible and trusted ambassador with auditors, advisors, donors, partners, community leaders, and other stakeholders, supporting the Foundation’s presence and mission across Canada.

What You Bring

You’re a strategic finance leader who pairs sound technical judgment with business curiosity and a hands-on approach. You move with ease between long-term vision and operational detail, helping leaders see the story behind the numbers and make bold, disciplined choices that bring the power of wishes to more children.

Proven Financial Leadership:
10+ years of progressive leadership in nonprofit financial management, with a track record of stewarding complex budgets, investments, assets, and financial operations in service of a bigger mission.

Strategic
Insight
:
Demonstrated strength in financial planning, forecasting, scenario analysis, and investment and treasury management, building the modelling capability that connects strategy, data, and execution.

Strong Credentials:
A CPA designation, supported by a bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, business, or a related field, equipping you to lead with rigour and credibility.

Governance and Compliance Expertise:
Advanced knowledge of nonprofit financial management, CRA requirements, GAAP, audits, internal controls, insurance, and board and committee governance — the discipline that protects trust in our mission.

Enterprise Risk and Business Operations Excellence:
Experience in enterprise risk management, business continuity, procurement, contracts, property, insurance, and service delivery across a national or multi-site organization, building a resilient foundation for growth.

Gift Administration Knowledge:
Experience overseeing restricted giving, endowments, estates, and other complex donation structures, with a deep understanding of donor stewardship and the financial processing that honours every gift.

Collaborative People Leadership:
A track record of recruiting, coaching, and developing multidisciplinary teams, building trust across functions and rallying people around shared goals.

Clear and Credible Communication:
The ability to turn complex financial and risk information into practical insight for executives, board members, auditors, volunteers, donors, and cross-functional partners.

Inspiring,
Values-Driven Leadership:
Deep alignment with our mission and a commitment to responsible stewardship, inclusion, and collaboration — a spirit that motivates teams, breaks down silos, and creates life-changing experiences for children and families facing critical illnesses.

How To Apply

If everything you’ve read so far sounds like you, we encourage you to apply
. Please visit the Make-A-Wish Canada candidate portal for current posting details and the application deadline.

Join Our Team - Make-A-Wish Canada

Make-A-Wish Canada
provides equal opportunity in employment and encourages applications from all qualified candidates. Reasonable accommodations due to disability are available on request at any stage of the hiring process.

OUR COMMITMENT TO IDEA

Make-A-Wish Canada is committed to Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, and Access (IDEA)
. We believe it is essential to our mission that we build a diverse, balanced, and vibrant workforce that reflects the communities we serve and seek to serve. Research has shown that candidates from underrepresented groups often apply only when they feel 100% qualified. Even if you do not see yourself fully reflected in every requirement, we still encourage you to apply.

RECRUITMENT PROCESS

Once applications are reviewed, shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Our typical process includes a phone screen, one or two interviews, reference checking, an offer, and a criminal background check for the successful candidate. We thank all applicants for their interest in working with us.

Job Description

Toast is recruiting for a 100% employee-owned Canadian consulting engineering firm with about 1,350 people. The firm is growing from “small” to “big” and is building out its Digital Services leadership. It has just finished a Microsoft Dynamics 365 implementation. Now it needs a Director, Enterprise Applications to take the platform from “live” to “working well,” and to bring in the best practices the organization doesn’t have yet.

You’ll lead three teams of about 16 people in total: the Dynamics Centre of Excellence, Application Development, and Applications Support. You’ll have room to shape the team, put structure in place, and build the technology roadmap. The firm wants a leader with executive polish who is also happy to roll up their sleeves, and who leads by bringing people along rather than by decree.

Responsibilities

Build and own a multi-year enterprise applications strategy and technology roadmap tied to business priorities
Lead the next phase of Dynamics 365 (Finance and Operations, Project Operations, HR, Customer Engagement), working through deferred scope and getting the most value out of the platform
Assess legacy applications and decide what to modernize, consolidate or retire
Set application development standards and governance, including secure development, source control, automated testing, CI/CD and Power Platform
Be the design authority for application, integration and platform architecture, working with Infrastructure, Enterprise Architecture, Cybersecurity, and Data and Reporting
Set the support operating model, service levels and release governance that keep production stable
Own the operating and capital budgets, licensing and total cost of ownership; lead vendor selection, RFPs, negotiations and renewals
Partner with leaders in Finance, HR, Operations, Project Delivery and other functions to turn business needs into roadmaps and investment decisions
Lead, coach and develop three Team Leads and their teams, with clear roles, career paths and a collaborative, service-focused culture

Requirements

10+ years of progressive experience in enterprise applications or business systems
Expert-level Microsoft Dynamics 365 experience, ideally including Finance and Operations and Project Operations
5+ years leading application teams at a senior manager or director level
Hands-on experience leading application development, with a strong grasp of modern development best practices
A track record of running large-scale enterprise applications, such as ERP or document management, through delivery, stabilization and sustainment. You need to have led the work, not just been part of it.
Experience building technology roadmaps and governance for application portfolios
Experience managing budgets, licensing, system integrators and software vendors

Nice to Haves

Experience in a multi-office engineering, consulting, professional services or project-based organization
Knowledge of Power Platform, Azure integrations, and Microsoft Fabric or Power BI
Experience setting up a Centre of Excellence or a platform governance model
Knowledge of project-based business processes such as project accounting, resourcing, time and expense, and billing
Dynamics 365, Power Platform, enterprise architecture or ITSM certifications

Benefits

Salary listed above, plus a matching company pension and annual salary reviews
The chance to become an owner at a 100% employee-owned firm
A newly shaped leadership role where you build the team, its structure and its roadmap
Health, dental and vision coverage, a fitness allowance and mental health supports
Generous vacation, plus a paid office closure over the December holidays
Paid professional development hours, formal mentoring and parental leave top-up
Application Review

Submit your application, including your resume and cover letter, through our online portal. Our team will carefully review your qualifications and experiences. We take pride in responding promptly, so if your application aligns with our current opportunities, you’ll hear back from us with next steps. Your journey with Toast begins here, and we’re excited to see what you bring to the table!

Vetting Call

If your application is successful, we’ll schedule a vetting call with a member of the Toast team. This 30-45 minute informal conversation is designed for us to get to know you better and assess your skills. Be prepared to discuss your past projects, the challenges you’ve tackled, and the impact you’ve made. This is your chance to shine and show us why you’re a great fit for the roles we offer.

Profile Creation

CONTEXT

At Make-A-Wish^® Canada
, we’re redefining how the world perceives wishes through our transformative new brand platform: Wishes Are Medicine.
Grounded in research, this platform recognizes what we’ve long known to be true — that wishes have measurable healing power. When prescribed alongside medical treatment, wishes reduce stress, elevate endorphins, limit emergency room visits, and deliver lasting health benefits.

With more than 3,500 children still waiting
and a new child diagnosed with a critical illness in Canada every two hours, our mission has never been more urgent — and there are many more prescriptions to fill.

To meet this challenge, we’ve launched our new three-year strategic plan — Wishes Are Medicine: One Team, One Mission
— focused intentionally on financial sustainability, mission impact, and operational excellence. When a child is facing a critical illness, a wish isn’t just a moment of joy — it’s a medically supported turning point. Studies show that children who receive a wish are 2.5 times less likely
to have unplanned hospital visits and 1.9 times less likely
to need the ER, with 100% of physicians agreeing that a wish can be a pivotal moment in treatment.

At Make-A-Wish Canada, you can play a lead role in bringing these powerful prescriptions to life. Where Wishes Are Medicine
, transformation becomes a pathway to healing at scale — and this role is your opportunity to architect that future.

Our ambition to reach more children and families requires a strong financial and operational foundation. As Vice President, Finance & Business Operations
, you will help shape that foundation, bringing strategic leadership to financial planning, investments, risk, governance and the services that enable our organization to thrive. You will turn insight into action, strengthen how resources are invested and managed, and help build a more resilient, disciplined and mission-driven organization.

At Make-A-Wish Canada

Every role — whether advancing fundraising, brand, operations, or technology — helps fuel the same trajectory: transforming how hope and healing come to life for children and families nationwide. If you’re ready to help build a future where every eligible child receives the wish that helps them heal, we invite you to read on.

Role Overview

We’re seeking a Vice President, Finance & Business Operations
, a strategic and forward-thinking leader who will help shape the next chapter of Make-A-Wish Canada. This is more than a finance role; it’s an opportunity to strengthen the financial and operational foundation that will enable our mission to grow sustainably.

As a key member of our Senior Leadership Team, and reporting to the Senior Vice President, Transformation & Operations, you will bring together financial strategy, business operations, analytics, risk and governance to strengthen how we plan, invest and make decisions. You’ll provide the insight and discipline to steward our resources responsibly, improve organizational performance, and build the capabilities needed to support sustainable growth and greater mission impact.

If you bring financial acumen, business curiosity and enterprise thinking, and believe the strongest organizations pair ambition with discipline, this is your opportunity to help build the foundation from which our mission can grow and bring the power of Wishes Are Medicine to more children and families across Canada.

This is a full-time, permanent, hybrid
role. The hiring range is $145,000-$170,000.

What You Will Do

Shape Financial Strategy:
Lead budgeting, forecasting, multi-year financial planning, and financial modelling. Translate insights into scenarios and recommendations that guide sustainable, mission-aligned decisions over a three-to-five-year time horizon.

Steward Assets and Investments:
Oversee financial assets, treasury, and investment portfolio performance in accordance with policy, ensuring disciplined stewardship and informed decision-making.

Strengthen Governance and Reporting:
Provide clear financial reporting to the Board of Directors and Senior Leadership Team, support the Finance & Audit Committee, and ensure sound governance, audit readiness, and compliance with CRA and other regulatory obligations.

Advance Enterprise Risk Management:
Maintain the enterprise risk register, strengthen internal controls, and lead business continuity and disaster recovery planning to protect the organization’s assets, reputation, and long-term sustainability.

Modernize Financial Capability:
Build stronger modelling, analytics, systems, and processes that improve forecasting, performance visibility, operational efficiency, and organizational decision-making.

Lead Business Services:
Oversee property management, leases, contracts, insurance, and related business services. Balance operational efficiency and financial sustainability with investments in organizational capability and a safe, supportive workplace.

Oversee Gift and Donation Administration:
Ensure sound systems and processes for restricted giving, endowments, estates, and other complex giving structures, coordinating closely with development teams to support stewardship and compliance.

Advise and Partner:
Serve as a trusted advisor to the Senior Vice President, Transformation & Operations, the CEO, and leadership colleagues on finance, risk, and business operations. Bring an enterprise lens to strategic planning and execution.

Guide and Develop Talent:
Build, coach, and lead a high-performing Finance and Business Operations team, creating clarity, accountability, collaboration, and opportunities for growth.

Model One Team, One Mission leadership by working across functions and geographies, breaking down silos, celebrating collective wins, and leading with empathy, inclusion, accountability, and purpose.

Represent the Mission:
Act as a visible and trusted ambassador with auditors, advisors, donors, partners, community leaders, and other stakeholders, supporting the Foundation’s presence and mission across Canada.

What You Bring

You’re a strategic finance leader who pairs sound technical judgment with business curiosity and a hands-on approach. You move with ease between long-term vision and operational detail, helping leaders see the story behind the numbers and make bold, disciplined choices that bring the power of wishes to more children.

Proven Financial Leadership:
10+ years of progressive leadership in nonprofit financial management, with a track record of stewarding complex budgets, investments, assets, and financial operations in service of a bigger mission.

Strategic
Insight
:

Strong Credentials:
A CPA designation, supported by a bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, business, or a related field, equipping you to lead with rigour and credibility.

Governance and Compliance Expertise:
Advanced knowledge of nonprofit financial management, CRA requirements, GAAP, audits, internal controls, insurance, and board and committee governance — the discipline that protects trust in our mission.

Enterprise Risk and Business Operations Excellence:
Experience in enterprise risk management, business continuity, procurement, contracts, property, insurance, and service delivery across a national or multi-site organization, building a resilient foundation for growth.

Gift Administration Knowledge:
Experience overseeing restricted giving, endowments, estates, and other complex donation structures, with a deep understanding of donor stewardship and the financial processing that honours every gift.

Collaborative People Leadership:
A track record of recruiting, coaching, and developing multidisciplinary teams, building trust across functions and rallying people around shared goals.

Clear and Credible Communication:
The ability to turn complex financial and risk information into practical insight for executives, board members, auditors, volunteers, donors, and cross-functional partners.

Inspiring,
Values-Driven Leadership:
Deep alignment with our mission and a commitment to responsible stewardship, inclusion, and collaboration — a spirit that motivates teams, breaks down silos, and creates life-changing experiences for children and families facing critical illnesses.
